subject: Clarifying SKU unification and plan interoperability for Skybridge pilot
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna@skybridge.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@skybridge.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SKU consolidation / interop question for pilot

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profile. Before we lock the pilot scope, procurement and our platform team asked for clarification on two things around packaging:

1) SKU consolidation: our SREs asked whether we can buy a single SKU that covers both hosted API traffic and dedicated pool capacity (we want a simple billing line during the pilot). Is that possible or do we need separate SKUs?

2) Plan interoperability: if we start with a compact pilot (metered tokens) and later want to move to a Dedicated pool with reserved throughput, what happens to the consumed credits/overages? Any proration or one-time conversion credits?

We also have a narrow ask — can you send a short matrix showing which features (live KV cache, per-route tracing, service accounts) are in which plan variant so we can show infra what they will get?

Appreciate a quick run-through so procurement can draft the PO.

—Anna
Anna Li
Head of Platform, Skybridge AI
anna@skybridge.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Li <anna@skybridge.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SKU consolidation / interop question for pilot

Hi Anna — great questions. Short answer up front: we can give you a simplified billing view for the pilot and a clear conversion path to Dedicated with a one-time credit, but there are a few knobs to set. Details below and I attached a compact SKU matrix and a proposal PDF for the pilot.

SKU consolidation options
- Single pilot SKU: includes hosted API + burstable Dedicated credit pool. This is a packaged pilot SKU (one invoice line), intended for 3 months. After pilot, you can either convert remaining credits into a Dedicated commit or roll into pay-as-you-go.
- Separate SKUs: Dedicated commit + hosted metered. This is cleaner for long-term procurement but more lines on the PO.

Conversion & credits
- If you convert from the pilot SKU to a Dedicated reservation within 60 days of pilot end, we offer a conversion credit equal to unused pilot credits *at a negotiated multiplier* (typical multiplier 0.6–0.8 depending on commit size).
- No automatic proration for historic billed metered usage; we credit only unapplied pilot credits.

Feature matrix (attached) highlights
- Live KV cache: included on Dedicated and on pilot SKU (restricted size).
- Per-route tracing: available as part of Redwood Console (retention depends on plan).
- Service accounts & VPC peering: require Private or Dedicated with enterprise controls.

Next steps
1) I included a short proposal (redwood-proposal-skybridge-v2.pdf) and an attached SKU matrix (sku-matrix-skybridge.xlsx).
2) Marissa (cc'ed) can jump in to confirm technical limits of the pilot's Dedicated burst window.
3) If procurement wants a single PO line, we can issue a pilot SKU quote and mark a conversion credit term in the SOW.

Will follow up with a one-page note you can attach to your PO.

Best,
Ben Carter

Ben — thanks, this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from our procurement and infra teams:

- Procurement: can you confirm language we can include in the PO that guarantees the conversion credit window (60 days) and the multiplier range? They want the legal phrasing to be short (1–2 lines).

- Infra: when you say "Dedicated burst window" for the pilot SKU, what are the hard limits (per-minute TPS, token/sec)? Our SREs also want to understand whether burst usage will throttle or fall back to hosted API if Dedicated pool is saturated.

If you can answer these two items we can finalize the PO draft this week. Also, is there an NDA appendix required for shared telemetry/trace logs?

Thanks — Anna

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Li <anna@skybridge.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SKU consolidation / interop question for pilot

Anna — quick answers and legal-friendly PO text below. Marissa added a tech note at the bottom.

Procurement wording (suggested PO line):
"Pilot SKU: Redwood Pilot Pack (Skybridge) — includes hosted API access and a 3-month burstable Dedicated credit pool; conversion to Dedicated reservation eligible for credit if conversion occurs within 60 days of pilot end (credit multiplier: 0.6–0.8 applied to unused pilot credits)."

Dedicated burst limits / runtime behavior:
- Hard limits for pilot SKU (default): 400 concurrent tokens/sec aggregate across pool; configurable by request (subject to capacity).
- If Dedicated burst pool is saturated, requests will automatically failover to hosted API variant within the same region (same model family) to preserve availability; telemetry will indicate fallback events in Redwood Console.

NDA / telemetry:
- We do not need a separate NDA for standard telemetry; we log traces for operational debugging. If Skybridge requires raw traces with PII removed or a separate custody agreement, we can add an appendix to the SOW.

Marissa's note (technical):
"Pilot burst windows are soft-limited; we can set a per-customer limiter in the serving layer and expose the throttling threshold in the Console. For production migration, we recommend running a 7-day soak with expected peak traffic to size the Dedicated commit and avoid conversion surprises."

Next steps:
- I'll update the proposal PDF with the PO wording and add the conversion clause.
- If procurement approves, send a draft PO and I'll route it to legal for a short SOW addendum.

Thanks — talk soon.

Ben
